title: Wendelin: special-mercy faith — future, present, and past remission as object
source_text: LXIII. Eodem modo plures alii Theologi varios actus distinguunt in fiducia illa, quae alias ab iis dicitur fides specialis misericordiae; & observant quosdam praecedere justificationem, quosdam vero minime. Istud videre est apud Wendelinum. Fides, inquit, specialis misericordiae, quantum praecedit justificationem (si modo tempore, & non ordine tantum praecedit) non credit homo sibi, jam ante fidei actum, remissa esse peccata, quoad applicationem; sed peccatorum remissionem Christi merito impetratam sibi quoque eventuram, in ipso justificationis actu credit peccata sibi remitti; & sic accipit remissionem peccatorum: Unde expressius dicitur peccatorum remissio accipi per fidem Act. 26. Post justificationem credit praeteritam applicationem; credit quoque sibi remissum iri futura peccata, per futuram applicationem. Habet igitur fides justificans pro objecto suo speciali, remissionem peccatorum futuram, praesentem, & praeteritam. Christ. Theolog. lib. 1. cap. 24. ad Thesin 11.
pass_a_gloss: In the same way several other Theologians distinguish various acts in that trust which is otherwise by them called faith of special mercy; and observe that some precede justification, but some by no means. That may be seen in Wendelin. Faith of special mercy, he says, insofar as it precedes justification (if indeed it precedes in time, and not only in order) — a man does not believe that sins have already been remitted to him before the act of faith as to application; but that the remission of sins obtained by Christ's merit will also come to him; in the very act of justification he believes sins are remitted to him; and so he receives remission of sins: Whence more expressly it is said that remission of sins is received by faith, Acts 26. After justification he believes the past application; he also believes that future sins will be remitted to him by future application. Justifying faith therefore has for its special object the remission of sins future, present, and past. Christian Theology book 1, chapter 24, on Thesis 11.
pass_b_english: Other Reformed also split special-mercy fiducia into acts before/after justification.
Wendelin: before the act, not ‘already remitted to me’; rather ‘will come to me’.
In the justifying act: believes sins are being remitted — receives remission (Acts 26).
Special object = remission future, present, and past.
